title: Sourdough Bread
subtitle: Open-crumb sourdough loaf with a crisp crust
excerpt: A proper sourdough loaf with a crackling crust and an open, chewy crumb, leavened with a wild yeast starter. A three-day project that rewards patience.

recipe.sourceNotes: Sourdough is the oldest form of leavened bread, dating back to ancient Egypt. Before commercial yeast became available in the nineteenth century, all bread was leavened with natural wild yeast cultures (starters) maintained from batch to batch. The sourdough starter (or levain) is a live culture of wild yeast and lactic acid bacteria maintained by regular feeding of flour and water. The slow fermentation process produces lactic and acetic acids which give sourdough its characteristic tang and also break down phytic acid in the flour, improving mineral absorption and making the gluten more digestible. A proper sourdough loaf requires several stages: building the levain, the autolyse rest, the bulk ferment with stretch and fold, shaping, and the final cold retard. This recipe uses a high hydration dough (75%) for an open crumb and is baked in a Dutch oven (casserole) to trap steam for a crisp, blistered crust.

recipeTools.notes: A cast-iron casserole or Dutch oven (24 cm) with a lid — essential for steam during baking.
A proving basket (banneton) is ideal; a bowl lined with a floured cloth works well.

content.text: The starter must be active and bubbly before you use it: feed it 8 to 12 hours before mixing and use it when it has risen and is full of bubbles. A starter that sinks or has a grey liquid layer on top needs feeding before use. The bulk ferment at room temperature takes 4 to 6 hours: the dough is done when it has grown by 50 to 75 per cent and a piece dropped into water floats. Bake in a preheated casserole at very high heat: the trapped steam prevents the crust forming too early and allows maximum oven spring.

items.preparation: active and bubbly; fed 8 to 12 hours before

content.text: Mix the flours with 375 ml of water (room temperature). Rest for 30 minutes (autolyse). Add the sourdough starter and salt. Squeeze and fold to fully incorporate. The dough will be sticky.

Bulk ferment at room temperature (20 to 24 C) for 4 to 6 hours. Every 30 minutes for the first 2 hours, perform a set of stretch and folds: pick up one side of the dough, stretch it up and fold it across. Rotate the bowl 90 degrees and repeat 4 times. After 4 stretch and fold sets, leave the dough to complete its rise undisturbed.
Shape the dough into a tight round and place seam-side up in a floured banneton or a bowl lined with a well-floured cloth. Cover and refrigerate for 10 to 16 hours.

Heat the oven to 250 C / fan 230 C with the casserole inside for 45 minutes. Turn the cold dough out onto a sheet of baking parchment. Score the top with a sharp blade. Lower into the hot casserole using the parchment. Cover with the lid. Bake for 20 minutes. Remove the lid and bake for a further 20 to 25 minutes until deep golden-brown. Cool for at least 1 hour before cutting.
